title: Going live
summary: Going live points your production CDN at the aem.live origin of the main branch. The checklist covers the checks before the switch, the CDN and invalidation setup, and what to watch in the weeks after launch.

items.title: Content and design QA
items.detail: Sign off content, design, accessibility and SEO on the .aem.live site, then freeze code and content location changes.

items.title: Lighthouse 100
items.detail: Score 100 on mobile and desktop in PageSpeed Insights on the .aem.live site before launch.

items.title: Telemetry early
items.detail: Add Operational Telemetry before launch so you can compare before and after metrics.

items.title: Analytics baseline
items.detail: Confirm martech tags fire and tell analysts that baselines like pageviews and bounce rate may shift.

items.title: Legacy redirects
items.detail: Add retired URLs to the redirects sheet, starting with the backlinks that matter most in Search Console.

items.title: Sitemap, robots, canonicals
items.detail: Serve a sitemap from the query index, check robots.txt, and make every canonical URL return 2xx.

items.title: CDN on main
items.detail: Point the production CDN at the main branch origin and 301 HTTP to HTTPS on apex and www.

items.title: Push invalidation tested
items.detail: Set up push invalidation for your CDN, publish a small change and see it on the production domain.

items.title: After launch
items.detail: Rerun PageSpeed Insights on production and watch Search Console and 404 reports for the following weeks.

title: Migrating a page
summary: Migrating turns an existing web page into content authors edit in EDS: docx, DA HTML or a JCR package. Getting the structure right on one page per type saves rework across every page you import after it.

items.title: One page per type
items.detail: Make an example import of each page type first and confirm authors find the structure intuitive.

items.title: Main content only
items.detail: Strip header, footer and other chrome; they come from nav and footer documents, not the page.

items.title: Simple for authors
items.detail: Use default content where it works and blocks only where needed, so authors can copy and understand them.

items.title: Rules in import.js
items.detail: Keep transformation rules in tools/importer/import.js so the same import repeats across many pages.

items.title: Right output format
items.detail: Save docx for Word or Google Docs, HTML for Document Authoring, or a JCR package for Universal Editor.

items.title: Import into drafts
items.detail: Import into a drafts folder first, since Experience Workspace import overwrites the destination.

items.title: Compare with original
items.detail: Preview the imported page locally and compare it with the source screenshot, with no console errors.

items.title: Read the report
items.detail: Check the bulk import report for 404s, 301s and failed pages before previewing them.

items.title: Redirect changed URLs
items.detail: Map the old URL 1-to-1 to the new one in the redirects sheet when the path changes.

title: Adding a block
summary: A block is a folder of JS and CSS named after the table authors type. Content-driven development means writing the test content first, then the code, then a PR with preview URLs the reviewer can open.

items.title: Check the collection
items.detail: Look in the Block Collection before building; reuse or extend an existing block when it fits.

items.title: Content first
items.detail: Write sample content before any code and have someone who supports authors review the structure.

items.title: Work in drafts
items.detail: Put test pages in /drafts/<yourname>/ rather than editing live pages.

items.title: Name matches folder
items.detail: Use the block name for the folder, the JS and CSS file names and the CSS class.

items.title: Variants as options
items.detail: Offer variations as block options in parentheses, which become extra classes on the block.

verify.how: read block JS for variant classes

items.title: Scoped CSS
items.detail: Prefix every selector with the block class so styles cannot leak into other blocks.

items.title: Backwards compatible
items.detail: Existing pages keep working after merge; new behavior appears only when authors republish content.

items.title: Checked in a browser
items.detail: View the block at mobile, tablet and desktop widths with no console errors.

items.title: PR with test URLs
items.detail: Open a PR with before and after test URLs; draft it while the content is still local.

title: Previewing & publishing
summary: Preview renders a page to .aem.page for review; publish copies that preview to .aem.live and production. Visitors only see what was published, so the checks happen on preview.

items.title: Preview from source
items.detail: Preview from the editor or Sidekick so .aem.page renders the latest version of the document.

items.title: Review on .aem.page
items.detail: Share the preview URL with stakeholders; it is not on your domain and search engines do not see it.

items.title: Run Preflight
items.detail: Run Preflight in Experience Workspace and fix failed checks before publishing.

items.title: Assets publishable
items.detail: Give images a file extension and supported type within size limits, and keep one valid JSON-LD block.

items.title: Know what changes
items.detail: Check Versions when the Send button shows an orange badge for previewed but unpublished changes.

items.title: Sheets published too
items.detail: Preview and publish changed redirects, placeholders or metadata sheets along with the pages.

items.title: Batch launches
items.detail: Group a launch's pages in a snapshot, review on .aem.reviews and publish them together.

items.title: Check production
items.detail: After publishing, open the page on the production domain to confirm the CDN serves the change.

title: Adding a locale
summary: A locale in EDS is a content folder, such as /fr/ or /en/uk/, with its own nav, footer and placeholders. Getting the URL structure, language markup and hreflang right up front avoids duplicate content and wrong-language links.

items.title: Language-first URLs
items.detail: Put language first and market second, such as /en/ and /en/uk/, unless markets share little content.

items.title: Only localized content
items.detail: Keep only pages that are actually localized in the market folder and fall back to the language folder.

items.title: Local nav and footer
items.detail: Copy nav and footer into the locale folder and make the code load the copy for that locale.

verify.how: open locale page, check nav links

items.title: Locale placeholders
items.detail: Keep a placeholders sheet in the locale root so UI strings are translated, not hard-coded.

items.title: Correct html lang
items.detail: Set the html lang per locale; the boilerplate scripts.js hard-codes 'en'.

items.title: hreflang in sitemap
items.detail: Configure the sitemap with each language's hreflang and alternate path.

items.title: Links stay in locale
items.detail: Rewrite links in content and code to the locale's version when that page exists.

items.title: Visitor can switch
items.detail: Let visitors choose a market and language and keep that choice on their device.

items.title: Translation workflow
items.detail: Use Experience Workspace translation projects or a connector rather than in-browser translation.

title: Going repoless
summary: Repoless lets many sites run off one GitHub repository, each with its own content source and configuration in the Configuration Service. Every code change reaches every site, so setup and testing need care.

items.title: Canonical site
items.detail: Keep one site whose org and site names match the GitHub owner and repo synced by AEM Code Sync.

items.title: Admin API access
items.detail: Get an Admin API access token before creating or changing site configurations.

items.title: Create site config
items.detail: Create each new site with the Admin API, pointing code at the shared repo and content at its own source.

items.title: Shared settings in profile
items.detail: Put shared headers, indexes and metadata in a profile; site settings win on conflict.

items.title: Config off files
items.detail: Move robots, headers, index and sitemap settings to the Configuration Service and remove the old files.

items.title: Preview new site
items.detail: Preview content on main--{site}--{org}.aem.page; it shows a 404 until something is previewed.

items.title: Local dev per site
items.detail: Run aem up --url with the site's preview URL to develop against its content.

items.title: Test across sites
items.detail: Check code changes on every site that shares the codebase, since a push applies to all of them.

items.title: Don't swap live code
items.detail: Never change code settings on a production site; create a new site and switch the CDN origin.

title: Retiring a page
summary: Retiring a page means unpublishing or deleting it and sending its traffic somewhere useful. Inbound links from search, social and bookmarks outlive the page, and unpublish and delete cannot be undone from Sidekick.

items.title: Pick next best page
items.detail: Choose a relevant replacement and avoid sending retired URLs to the homepage.

items.title: Add a redirect
items.detail: Add a Source and Destination row to the redirects sheet, check it on .aem.page, then publish.

items.title: Fix internal links
items.detail: Update nav, fragments and pages that link to the retired URL.

items.title: Unpublish
items.detail: Unpublish from Sidekick to remove the page from live and production; it needs the publish role.

items.title: Delete or archive source
items.detail: Delete the source document or move it to drafts, then delete the preview if it is not needed.

items.title: Gone from index
items.detail: Confirm the page left query-index.json and the sitemap, which list published pages only.

items.title: Double-check first
items.detail: Confirm the URL before unpublish or delete; neither can be undone from Sidekick.

items.title: Watch 404s
items.detail: Monitor 404s in Operational Telemetry after retiring pages and add redirects as needed.

title: Reviewing a pull request
summary: Merging to main deploys to production through AEM Code Sync, so the pull request is the release gate. The reviewer opens the branch preview, checks the PageSpeed and lint results, and reads the diff against EDS conventions.

items.title: Issue and test URLs
items.detail: The description links the issue and gives before and after test URLs on main and the branch.

items.title: Branch preview loads
items.detail: Open {branch}--{repo}--{owner}.aem.page; the whole host part has to fit in 63 characters.

items.title: PSI check green
items.detail: The Code Sync PageSpeed Insights check passes on mobile and desktop, ideally at 100.

items.title: Lint passes
items.detail: ESLint and Stylelint pass in the PR check, without loosened lint rules.

items.title: Scope matches title
items.detail: The diff covers only what the title says, with no reformatting noise; unfinished work stays draft.

items.title: Block code isolated
items.detail: Block CSS selectors are scoped to the block and third-party scripts load in the block, not head.html.

items.title: Existing content safe
items.detail: Existing pages render as before; new behavior only appears with new content.

items.title: Author merges
items.detail: Approve, then let the author merge when ready, since merging to main deploys to production.

title: Rolling back
summary: Rolling back in EDS means reverting code in git or restoring a content version and republishing it. Code merges to main and publishes purge the caches; a manual purge exists for when they don't.

items.title: Code or content
items.detail: Decide if the regression came from a merge to main or from a publish, and roll back that side only.

items.title: Revert in git
items.detail: Revert the merge on main through a PR; Code Sync deploys main to production.

items.title: Keep site config
items.detail: Do not repoint a production site's code config; create a new site and switch the CDN origin.

items.title: Restore a version
items.detail: In Experience Workspace, restore the last good version from Versions, then preview and publish it.

items.title: Bring back a page
items.detail: Restore the deleted source document, then preview and publish it again.

items.title: Republish sheets
items.detail: Restore and republish redirects, placeholders or metadata sheets if they caused the issue.

items.title: Purge if stale
items.detail: If production still serves old content, purge it with the Admin API cache endpoint.

items.title: Confirm on production
items.detail: Check the fix on the production domain as well as .aem.live, since a BYO CDN relies on push invalidation.
